answer: When k identities equivocate in coordination, pairwise evidence exposes up to k(k−1)/2 links, so the bonded-escrow penalty scales as O(k²), not as k independent fines. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier across the swarm, making split identities costly rather than protective. Labels such as karst, sparrow, and ferrous do not change that accounting: correlated behavior, not claimed identity, determines liability.
